events.title: World Rhythm Festival
events.desc: This festival has a captivating weekend lineup. Bring (or borrow!) a drum to join Friday night’s opening drum circle, then come back Saturday and Sunday for traditional performances and engaging workshops. The festival takes place at the Rainier Arts Center, Southside Commons and Columbia Park — all within walking distance of each other.

events.title: Mukilteo Lighthouse Festival
events.loc: Mukilteo Lighthouse Park , 609 Front St., Mukilteo
events.desc: Bounce into the weekend on giant inflatables at this beloved annual fest. It celebrates local history and (objectively speaking) one of the cutest lighthouses in the region. Saturday brings a parade, fireworks, and special appearances from the Reptile Lady and Bubble Man. On Sunday, you can catch performances from Thee Balloon Guy and Savanna Woods.

events.title: Venardos Circus Presents ‘Far Beyond’
events.desc: Step under the big top and prepare to be amazed by the high-flying aerial acts of Vernardos Circus. In this all-new production, you can expect theatrical music and exciting performances including juggling and acrobatics. From what I’ve heard, there’s not a bad seat in the house.

events.title: Salmon on Sunset Celebration
events.loc: Issaquah Salmon Hatchery , 125 W. Sunset Way, Issaquah
events.desc: At the very top of my fall bucket list this year, you’ll find salmon viewing. I am so looking forward to cheering on these triumphant fish as they swim upstream. This seasonal celebration is the perfect place to do just that, with family-friendly activities including arts and crafts. Come for the salmon, stay for the rubber duck derby.

events.title: Emily’s Science Lab Live
events.cost: Included with admission ($21-$29; ages 4 and younger free) or membership
events.loc: The Museum of Flight , 9404 E. Marginal Way S., Seattle
events.desc: Excuse me while I fangirl out for a moment: The Space Gal, Emily Calandrelli, will be bringing her science lab to The Museum of Flight this weekend. Watch as she experiments with slime, bubbles and more. And stick around to purchase her bestselling book and get your copy signed. Note that there is limited seating for the show, and it is first come, first served. Get there early!

events.title: Touch-A-Truck
events.loc: Sprinker Recreation Center , 14824 C St. S., Tacoma
events.desc: Beep, beep! Big trucks are coming through. Kids can explore a fire engine, semi trucks, search and rescue vehicles, a garbage truck and more, all while chatting with the truck operators. There’s a special no-horns time scheduled from noon to 1 p.m. You’ll also want to plan for extra time on the rec center’s thrilling playgrounds — it’s one of my favorites.

events.title: Burien Arts-A-Glow Festival
events.loc: Town Square Park , 480 S.W. 152nd St., Burien
events.desc: Spend a night out on the town and see Burien in a new light during this glowing art festival. You can expect light installations, projection mapping on buildings, wandering performers and special hands-on activities. There will also be a night market.

events.title: Tacoma Moon Festival
events.loc: Chinese Reconciliation Park , 1741 N. Shuster Pkwy., Tacoma
events.desc: This fantastic event is an opportunity to learn about and celebrate the traditions of the Mid-Autumn Festival. There will be stage performances, crafts and more family-friendly activities, all in a beautiful local park. Kids will especially love the legend of the Chinese Moon Princess — she leads a lantern parade at the end of the festival.

events.title: BrickCon 2026
events.cost: $19–$24 per person; children 4 and younger are free
events.loc: Meydenbauer Center , 11100 N.E. Sixth St., Bellevue
events.desc: BrickCon is the longest-running Lego fan convention in the world, and it’s celebrating its 25th year! There will be hundreds of creations on display this weekend, from trains and spaceships to full cities. You can even check out new Pokémon Lego sets, learn how to build robots and add to the mosaic wall. Buy your timed tickets in advance and prepare to be amazed.

events.title: Free Day at Wing Luke Museum
events.loc: Wing Luke Museum , 719 S. King St., Seattle
events.desc: Wing Luke Museum is offering free admission in honor of Grandparents Day, but you don’t have to be a grandparent to enjoy it! You’ll get access to the museum’s incredible exhibits, take a guided museum tour, and join special programming with “Ten Thousand Things” curator, Shin Yu Pai. Note that advance registration is required.
